subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 29-year-old woman presents with 3 weeks of depressed mood most of the day and loss of interest in her usual activities. She has difficulty falling asleep, feels worthless, has little energy, cannot concentrate, has gained 4 kg, and has thoughts that she would be better off dead. She reports no periods of elevated mood.
question: Which of the following best describes the diagnostic threshold for a major depressive episode in this patient?

options.text: At least two depressive symptoms for at least 1 year
At least three symptoms for at least 1 week, including increased energy
At least five symptoms for at least 1 week, regardless of mood
At least five of nine symptoms for at least 2 weeks, including depressed mood or anhedonia
At least four symptoms for at least 2 days with a clear stressor

explanation_correct: A major depressive episode lasts at least 2 weeks and requires at least five of nine symptoms, including depressed mood or loss of interest or pleasure (anhedonia; irritability in children). The SIG E CAPS mnemonic captures the symptoms: Sleep changes, loss of Interest, Guilt or worthlessness, decreased Energy, decreased Concentration, Appetite or weight changes, Psychomotor retardation or agitation, and Suicidal ideation. This patient has depressed mood, anhedonia, sleep disturbance, guilt, low energy, poor concentration, appetite and weight change, and suicidal thoughts.

explanation_incorrect.A: Two symptoms for 2 years describes persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia), not a major depressive episode.
explanation_incorrect.B: Three symptoms for 1 week does not meet the threshold for depression; that count and duration more closely resemble the symptom requirement for mania.
explanation_incorrect.C: Major depression requires at least 2 weeks and must include depressed mood or anhedonia, not simply any five symptoms within 1 week.
explanation_incorrect.E: Four symptoms for 2 days is insufficient in both number and duration for a major depressive episode.

educationalObjective: A major depressive episode requires at least five of nine SIG E CAPS symptoms for 2 weeks or more, including depressed mood or anhedonia.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 26-year-old man presents with 4 weeks of depressed mood, anhedonia, fatigue, and difficulty concentrating. Before starting an antidepressant, his psychiatrist asks detailed questions about any past periods of unusually elevated mood, decreased need for sleep, or impulsive behavior.
question: Which of the following best explains the purpose of this questioning?

options.text: To assess for a history of substance use disorder before prescribing medication
To determine whether electroconvulsive therapy will be required
To rule out bipolar disorder, because antidepressants can precipitate mood destabilization
To evaluate for a psychotic disorder before starting an SSRI
To establish eligibility for psychotherapy rather than medication

explanation_correct: Before treating a major depressive episode, clinicians must screen for previous manic or hypomanic episodes to rule out bipolar disorder. Antidepressants can destabilize mood in bipolar patients, and treating bipolar depression with an antidepressant alone risks precipitating mania or hypomania. Identifying a prior elevated episode would change both the diagnosis and the treatment plan.

explanation_incorrect.A: Although substance use is relevant in depression, questions about elevated mood and decreased sleep are specifically aimed at detecting mania or hypomania, not substance use.
explanation_incorrect.B: ECT is an effective treatment for severe depression, but screening questions about mood elevation are not used to decide on ECT.
explanation_incorrect.D: Psychotic symptoms are assessed separately; asking about elevated mood and impulsivity is specifically intended to rule out bipolar disorder.
explanation_incorrect.E: The questioning is diagnostic, not a determination of whether psychotherapy or medication is the appropriate modality.

educationalObjective: Always screen for prior mania or hypomania before diagnosing and treating major depression, because antidepressants can destabilize mood in bipolar disorder.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 45-year-old woman has had 6 weeks of profound depressed mood, anhedonia, and guilt. She believes she is being punished for unpardonable sins and that her internal organs are rotting away. She hears voices telling her she deserves to die. These symptoms occur only during the depressive episode; between episodes she has no psychotic symptoms and functions normally.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Schizophrenia with depressive features
Major depressive disorder with mood-congruent psychotic features
Schizoaffective disorder, depressive type
Delusional disorder, somatic type
Bipolar I disorder, current episode depressed

explanation_correct: Major depressive disorder with psychotic features involves a major depressive episode plus hallucinations or delusions. The psychotic features are typically mood congruent, with depressive themes of inadequacy, guilt, punishment, nihilism, disease, or death — as in this patient's beliefs about punishment and bodily decay. Crucially, the psychotic symptoms occur only in the context of the major depressive episode; between episodes she has none. Treatment is an antidepressant with an atypical antipsychotic, or ECT.

explanation_incorrect.A: Schizophrenia requires at least 6 months of illness including 1 month of active symptoms and psychosis that is not confined to mood episodes; her psychosis occurs only during depression.
explanation_incorrect.C: Schizoaffective disorder requires at least 2 weeks of psychotic symptoms in the absence of a mood episode; her psychotic symptoms remit entirely between depressive episodes.
explanation_incorrect.D: Delusional disorder involves at least one delusion for more than 1 month without other psychotic symptoms or a mood disorder; she has hallucinations, mood symptoms, and multiple delusional themes.
explanation_incorrect.E: Bipolar I disorder requires at least one manic episode; she has no history of elevated mood or mania.

educationalObjective: Psychotic features in MDD are typically mood congruent with guilt, punishment, nihilism, or death themes and occur only during the depressive episode, distinguishing it from schizoaffective disorder.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 38-year-old man reports feeling mildly depressed for most of the past 4 years. He describes low energy, difficulty concentrating, and low self-esteem. He has never been completely symptom-free for more than 1 month at a time. He continues to work and maintain relationships, though he feels he is just going through the motions. He has never had a manic episode.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Major depressive disorder
Bipolar II disorder
Cyclothymic disorder
Generalized anxiety disorder
Persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia)

explanation_correct: Persistent depressive disorder, also called dysthymia, involves at least two depressive symptoms lasting at least 2 years (at least 1 year in children), with any remission lasting no more than 2 months. It is often milder than major depressive disorder, and functioning is generally preserved, as in this patient. The absence of hypomanic episodes excludes cyclothymia and bipolar II.

explanation_incorrect.A: Major depressive disorder requires discrete episodes of at least 2 weeks with five or more symptoms; his symptoms are chronic, milder, and have lasted 4 years with only brief remissions.
explanation_incorrect.B: Bipolar II disorder requires at least one hypomanic episode plus a major depressive episode; he has no hypomania.
explanation_incorrect.C: Cyclothymic disorder requires at least 2 years of both mild hypomanic and mild depressive symptoms; he has only depressive symptoms.
explanation_incorrect.D: Generalized anxiety disorder involves excessive worry about multiple domains for at least 6 months, not a chronic depressed mood with low energy and low self-esteem.

educationalObjective: Persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia) is at least 2 years of two or more depressive symptoms with remission no longer than 2 months and relatively preserved function.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 34-year-old woman has noticed that every November she becomes depressed, sleeps more, gains weight, and loses interest in activities. These episodes last until March, when her mood spontaneously improves. Similar episodes have occurred each winter for the past 5 years, with no manic symptoms at any time.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis and recommended treatment addition?

options.text: Major depressive disorder with seasonal pattern; add light therapy
Persistent depressive disorder; begin lithium monotherapy
Bipolar II disorder; start an SSRI as monotherapy
Generalized anxiety disorder; begin benzodiazepine therapy
Atypical depression; begin a monoamine oxidase inhibitor as first-line treatment

explanation_correct: MDD with a seasonal pattern, formerly called seasonal affective disorder, consists of major depressive episodes occurring only during a particular season — usually winter — for at least 2 consecutive years and in most years across a lifetime. Atypical symptoms such as hypersomnia and hyperphagia are common. Treatment is standard MDD therapy plus light therapy.

explanation_incorrect.B: Persistent depressive disorder is a chronic, nonseasonal condition lasting at least 2 years; the episodic winter pattern with full remission points to seasonal MDD, and lithium is not the indicated addition.
explanation_incorrect.C: Bipolar II requires hypomanic episodes, which she has never had; moreover, an SSRI alone can destabilize mood in bipolar disorder.
explanation_incorrect.D: Generalized anxiety disorder involves chronic excessive worry, not recurrent seasonal depressive episodes with neurovegetative symptoms.
explanation_incorrect.E: Although atypical features are common in seasonal depression, MAO inhibitors are effective but not first line because of their risk profile; light therapy is the recommended addition.

educationalObjective: Seasonal MDD features winter-predominant depressive episodes for at least 2 consecutive years, commonly with atypical symptoms, and is treated with standard MDD therapy plus light therapy.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 28-year-old woman has had several episodes of depression. Notably, her mood temporarily brightens when a friend visits or when she receives good news, though it returns to baseline soon afterward. During episodes she sleeps 10 to 12 hours a day, craves carbohydrates and gains weight, and feels a heavy, leaden sensation in her arms and legs. She has been extremely sensitive to perceived rejection since adolescence. She has no history of mania.
question: Which of the following statements about this patient's depression is most accurate?

options.text: Mood reactivity excludes a major depressive episode, so this represents normal sadness
These features are most consistent with melancholic depression, which is the most common subtype
The presence of leaden paralysis and rejection sensitivity indicates a psychotic disorder
This is the most common subtype of depression, and MAO inhibitors are effective but not first-line because of their risk profile
Atypical features require immediate electroconvulsive therapy

explanation_correct: Depression with atypical features is characterized by mood reactivity (transient improvement in response to positive events), hypersomnia, hyperphagia, leaden paralysis (a heavy feeling in the arms and legs), and long-standing interpersonal rejection sensitivity. It is the most common subtype of depression. CBT and SSRIs are first line; MAO inhibitors are effective but not first line because of their risk profile.

explanation_incorrect.A: Mood reactivity is a defining feature of atypical depression and does not exclude a major depressive episode; she has multiple other neurovegetative symptoms.
explanation_incorrect.B: Melancholic depression features anhedonia and lack of mood reactivity, the opposite of this presentation; atypical depression is the most common subtype.
explanation_incorrect.C: Leaden paralysis and rejection sensitivity are characteristic of atypical depression, not a psychotic disorder; there are no hallucinations or delusions.
explanation_incorrect.E: ECT is reserved for severe, treatment-resistant, or psychotic depression, not routinely for atypical features; CBT and SSRIs are first line.

educationalObjective: Atypical depression features mood reactivity, hypersomnia, hyperphagia, leaden paralysis, and rejection sensitivity; it is the most common subtype, with CBT/SSRIs first line and MAOIs effective but not first line.
